extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral and experienced researchers from Germany (or integrated in the German academic system) applying for the Feodor Lynen Research Fellowship
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and selection criteria for applying to the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation's Feodor Lynen Research Fellowship (postdoctoral and experienced researcher tracks), including eligibility rules, required documents, host and reviewer requirements, selection criteria, and procedural timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality / principal residence / integration in German system
rubrics_metrics.description: You hold German citizenship. If not German, you are eligible only if you are working academically in Germany at the time of application and already integrated into the German academic system and intend to return to it after the stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a rule integration means at least five years working in Germany in a scientific capacity or having completed school and university education (or doctorate) in Germany and Germany is your principal country of residence and work at time of application. If only in Germany for doctoral purposes or integrated in a foreign system, you are not eligible. Contact info@avh.de if in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on prior stays in the host country
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible you must not have spent more than six months in total in the selected host country within the 18-month period prior to submitting your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a formal condition; the relevant deadline is the date the Humboldt Foundation receives your application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time since doctorate — postdoctoral researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdocs: You must have completed your doctorate within the last four years or be within six months of completion with written summary of findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If selected, you must complete your doctorate before commencing the fellowship. Applications will be rejected for formal reasons if the dissertation hasn't been published and you have no further academic publications at time of application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time since doctorate — experienced researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Experienced researchers: You must have completed your doctorate within the last twelve years and have an extensive publication record demonstrating an independent academic profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you completed your doctorate more than twelve years ago exceptions may be made in well-founded cases (e.g., recognised parental leave) — contact info@avh.de with CV and publication list for advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of career breaks (child-rearing, illness, service)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognised career breaks after the doctorate (child-rearing, military/alternative service, care for relatives, long-term illness, institute closures such as lockdown) may be taken into account to extend eligibility timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mothers can claim two extra years for each child born after the PhD plus other verifiable parenting periods; fathers/others credited for verifiable parenting periods. Extensions are limited to six years in total. Job hunting, unemployment and non-academic employment do not count as career breaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunities and contextual assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of academic achievements is made on an individual basis and may consider personal circumstances and structural barriers (e.g., difficult research conditions, gender-specific discrimination, cultural barriers to mobility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voluntary disclosure of private circumstances in the application may help achieve a fairer assessment. See Humboldt Foundation's equal opportunities statement for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host eligibility (who can act as academic host)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your host must be a member of the Humboldt Network abroad or a recipient of a specified international academic award working abroad and be firmly established abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hosts include former Humboldt awardees, those who have supervised Humboldt-sponsored researchers, former selection committee members, participants in Frontiers of Research Symposia, or holders of specified international awards. Individuals with close personal/familial relationships (parents, siblings, children, spouses/partners) cannot be hosts. The Foundation can verify host eligibility on request and provides a host search tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host's statement and confirmation of research facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: An eligible academic host must provide written confirmation that research facilities are available, submit a mentoring agreement, and compile a detailed review for the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host's statement and confirmation must be uploaded by the host personally in a protected area. The host's statement does not count as an expert review. Applications cannot be submitted until host and expert reviewers have uploaded their documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host financial contribution expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Humboldt Foundation expects the host to participate in financing the fellowship, generally amounting to approximately one third of the fellowship amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement is waived for hosts from certain countries (see list of countries). In cases of documented funding issues, exceptions or individual solutions may be explored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required expert reviews (number and purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must provide two expert reviews which assess your development as a researcher, your potential, and your academic accomplishments to date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expert reviews should be well grounded and reviewers well acquainted with your work; they are usually requested by the Foundation for independent peer review and are submitted directly by reviewers into a secure protected area. Reviews should not be more than 12 months old at time of application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who should provide expert reviews (postdocs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral applicants: reviews should be from the doctoral supervisor and one other researcher — preferably from outside your own institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The host's statement does not count as an expert review. You are responsible for requesting the expert reviews and ensuring they are uploaded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who should provide expert reviews (experienced researchers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Experienced researchers: reviews should be provided by important collaborative partners and/or researchers at your own institute and other institutes, including collaborators from outside Germany if possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reviews come from persons who can evaluate your independent academic profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language skills
rubrics_metrics.description: You must have a good knowledge of the language of your host country, or at least an excellent command of English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No formal language certificate is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of prior Humboldt sponsorship
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not apply if you have already received sponsorship from the Humboldt Foundation (alumni programmes are open instead).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If previously sponsored, use alumni programmes for support; contacting the Foundation for guidance is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications — peer-reviewed standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have been published in academic journals and by publishing houses that are reviewed according to international standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation emphasises international peer-review standards when assessing publication quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key publications — number and selection rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdocs: cite 1–3 key publications (one sufficient). Experienced researchers: cite 3–5 key publications (minimum three).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key publications should present your most important academic results, reflect recent publication activity where possible, and indicate your personal contribution in multi-author works. You cannot change key publications once the selection process has begun; surplus key publications will be removed without notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete list of publications — requirements and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: You must upload a complete list of publications (format guidance via sample list) including the key publications; accuracy in authorship order, titles and venues is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inaccurate information could lead to formal rejection. The key publications should also appear in the complete list. Once the selection process has started, it is not possible to amend the publication lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication status rules (what may be cited)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only cite publications that are already in print, accepted for publication, or at least submitted to a publishing house. Dissertation/habilitation may be cited as a key publication even if not yet submitted for print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For submitted publications include acknowledgement of receipt from the publisher; for accepted ones include the letter of acceptance. Other works will be deleted. Unpublished dissertations/habilitations may be uploaded as original manuscripts if cited as key publications; dissertations may not be listed in the complete list if unpublished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research outline requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: You must discuss details of your independently developed research outline with your chosen academic host before applying and submit a research outline (five pages max).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed research should demonstrate originality, innovative potential, significance for the development of the subject area, a convincing selection of scientific methods, potential for scientific development, clear focus and feasibility within the requested sponsorship period, and viability at the host institute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria used by reviewers and committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment is based on: academic career and record to date (mobility, determination, thematic scope, academic productivity); quality of key publications (originality, innovativeness, evaluation of your own contribution); originality and innovative potential of the proposed research (significance, methods, focus, feasibility, viability); future potential (academic potential, personal development, career prospects); and, for experienced researchers, independent research profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection committee decisions are usually based on two independent peer reviews and the committee (approx. 20 researchers across disciplines) decides by majority vote. Assessment considers individual life journeys and equal opportunities/accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility and focus within requested sponsorship period
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed research must have a clear focus and be feasible within the requested fellowship period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection reviewers evaluate whether the scientific methods and project scope are realistic for the length of sponsorship requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship duration rules (postdocs and experienced researchers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdocs: 6–24 month fellowship (first stay must be at least six months and the research stay cannot be broken up). Experienced researchers: 6–18 month fellowship which can be split into up to three stays over three years (must follow programme's model).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deviations from the standard model for experienced researchers are not permitted; postdocs cannot split the stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness and protected upload of host/reviewer documents
rubrics_metrics.description: You may only submit your application once you have uploaded required documents and the host and expert reviewers have personally uploaded their documents in the secure protected area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You will be notified automatically when all documents have been uploaded; incomplete applications take longer to process or may be postponed. Expert reviews should be no older than 12 months at time of application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review timing, deadlines and processing time
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection Committee meets three times a year (February, June, October). Applications should be submitted well in advance (normally 4–7 months ahead) and are processed within about four to seven months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are processed on an ongoing basis and forwarded to independent peer reviewers when complete. The date used to determine eligibility formal conditions is the date the Foundation receives the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification, feedback, and re-application rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and hosts are notified by email after the selection meeting; if rejected, applicants may request informal feedback on reasons (usually provided ~4–6 weeks after selection meeting). Re-application is possible but the new application should differ significantly from the rejected one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experience suggests waiting about two years to re-apply after strengthening the academic profile (e.g., new publications). Submitting a new application that differs little may result in formal rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start date and retroactivity rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If successful, the fellow may begin the fellowship between two and twelve months after selection (minimum 2 and maximum 12 months); the fellowship cannot be paid retroactively if you are already at the host institute at time of selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visa requirements may lengthen preparation time. You must start within twelve months or you will have to submit a new application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family allowances and childcare support
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional funding is available for fellows accompanied by family: family allowance for partner, child allowance if children accompany, and possible childcare support (e.g., subsidy for childcare costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Family members must accompany the fellow for more than three months to qualify for allowances. Travel expenses for family members can be covered if they accompany the fellow for at least six months; check fellowship calculator and programme guidelines for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel reimbursement and travel cost rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel expenses are reimbursed in addition to the fellowship amount; if the fellow's own institution does not cover travel, the Foundation will pay a single lump sum for return travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Travel expenses for accompanying family members may be covered under specific conditions (see family allowances guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent applications restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not possible to apply to several Humboldt Foundation fellowship programmes or the Sofja Kovalevskaja Award concurrently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel external applications to other institutions are possible but must be declared on the application form and the Foundation must be informed of any other sponsorship decisions while the application is under consideration.
